purpose: Production NVIDIA Jetson Thor modules and a deployment carrier platform relevant to high-capacity local LLM, VLM, robotics, and DC-powered edge inference.
notes: The Jetson T4000 and T5000 are production system-on-modules, not developer kits. They require a compatible carrier board, storage, cooling, and power subsystem.
FP4 TFLOPS figures are NVIDIA sparse vendor metrics and are not directly comparable with dense FP16/FP32 throughput or tokens per second.
Model-fit guidance is capacity-oriented. Actual usable model size and generation speed depend on runtime, quantization, KV cache, context length, and workload.
Retail prices are point-in-time observations and should not be treated as MSRP unless explicitly stated.

hardware.cooling: Integrated thermal-transfer plate; carrier/system must provide an appropriate heatsink or forced-air solution.
hardware.quantization_support_notes: Blackwell Tensor Cores support low-precision inference paths including FP4 through NVIDIA software; GGUF/llama.cpp compatibility depends on current Jetson CUDA builds rather than the FP4 headline metric alone.
hardware.llm_fit: 64GB unified memory can host many 30B-class quantized models and selected larger low-bit models. It is especially attractive when 64GB capacity is enough and the 70W module ceiling matters more than T5000's extra memory.
hardware.performance_per_watt_notes: At the maximum 70W module setting, the 273GB/s memory subsystem corresponds to about 3.90 GB/s of memory bandwidth per module watt. This is a simple ratio, not an application benchmark.

availability_lifecycle.note: NVIDIA Jetson product lifecycle page lists T4000 availability through January 2036.

pricing.note: Waveshare's shared T4000/T5000 selector displayed US$3,599 with an out-of-stock state at observation time. Treat this as a retailer observation, not NVIDIA MSRP.

hardware.cooling: Integrated thermal-transfer plate; carrier/system must provide an appropriate heatsink or forced-air solution.
hardware.quantization_support_notes: Blackwell Tensor Cores support low-precision inference including FP4 through NVIDIA's software stack. GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ, FP8, and FP4 practicality varies by engine and model and should be benchmarked per runtime.
hardware.llm_fit: 128GB unified memory is sufficient for many 70B-class quantized models with substantial KV-cache headroom and enables selected larger low-bit or MoE experiments. Decode remains constrained by the 273GB/s memory subsystem compared with HBM/GDDR workstation accelerators.
hardware.performance_per_watt_notes: At the maximum 130W module setting, 273GB/s corresponds to about 2.10 GB/s of memory bandwidth per module watt. Lower power modes may improve energy efficiency at reduced throughput.

availability_lifecycle.note: NVIDIA Jetson product lifecycle page lists T5000 availability through August 2035.

pricing.note: Waveshare listed the T5000 option at US$6,419 in the current product result. Retailer pricing is dynamic and is not NVIDIA MSRP.

hardware.product: reComputer J601 Carrier Board / Robotics J6014-J6015 Platform
storage: 1x M.2 Key M PCIe Gen4 NVMe 2280
hardware.cooling: 4-pin 12V PWM fan connector; Seeed sells a matching heatsink/fan bundle.
hardware.llm_fit: Carrier/platform rather than a compute architecture. With T4000 it provides a DC-native 64GB Blackwell node; with T5000 it provides a DC-native 128GB node. The 19-48V input, multi-10GbE connectivity, NVMe slot, and robotics I/O make it more deployment-oriented than NVIDIA's desktop-style developer kit.

pricing.note: Seeed sells the J601 as a configurable bundle with carrier, heatsink/fan, T4000 or T5000 module, storage, power supply, and optional wireless hardware. The displayed total changes with selections, so no single numeric price is stored as a durable platform price.
